newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar strengthens slightly in heavy trades.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar strengthens slightly in heavy trades.

text.p: The Canadian dollar strengthened slightly Thursday in active trading to C$1.3702 (US$0.7299) from Wednesday's close at C$1.3712 (US$0.7293).
Dealers said Canadian corporations made up much of the buying activity.
"Corporate Canada was busy, but not a lot of trading range," said Reid Farrill, foreign exchange specialist at CIBC. "There's a reasonable amount of corporate hedging going on."
The currency is likely to stick to a narrow trading range until next week, dealers said.
The market has its eye on Tuesday's U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
Recent U.S. economic data has sparked fears the Fed will raise rates, undermining any solid gains by the Canadian dollar, dealers said.
In economic news, Statistics Canada is to release retail trade statistics on Friday morning.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar firmed to 1.040 marks from Wednesday's close of 1.1000 marks and rose to 79.78 yen from 79.56 yen.
